legacy_screen.method: fresh repository search for CVR/contingent-value-right/Atossa/priority-review-voucher terminology plus comparison with existing event candidate
legacy_screen.distinct_from: EVENT-DUEBILL-LARGE-DIST-001 is a large-distribution/due-bill mechanism; this candidate concerns a contractually stapled contingent right whose value remains attached to each common share until discretionary detachment or expiry.

primary_document.source: SEC EDGAR 8-K for Atossa Therapeutics filed 2026-10-09
document_facts: Board declared one stapled CVR for each common share outstanding at close of business 2026-10-19.
Each stapled CVR represents a contractual claim to a pro-rata share of a CVR payment tied to the first qualifying priority review voucher, capped in aggregate at USD 50m.
Until detachment, CVRs transfer only together with common shares and have no separate CUSIP or separate trading market.
The board may detach the CVRs in its sole discretion; detached rights may never obtain a trading market.
No qualifying voucher had been awarded as of the filing and the company had not submitted a marketing application for the referenced program.

candidate_hypothesis.claim: A newly declared, non-separately-tradable contingent value right stapled to common equity creates a mechanically identifiable embedded-claim interval in which common-share valuation must jointly reflect operating equity and a highly uncertain contractual contingent asset. A future authorized test may ask whether documented changes in the attached-right state (attachment, detachment announcement, expiry, or qualifying monetization) create reproducible valuation dislocations, but this generation makes no directional return claim.
causal_chain: contract creates one attached CVR per eligible common share
attached CVR cannot initially be separately traded or independently price-discovered
common share therefore bundles operating equity with contingent contractual payoff exposure
state transitions in attachment/detachment/qualifying-voucher status alter the composition or observability of that bundled claim
any economic effect, if one exists, must survive independent validation and a separately authorized frozen outcome protocol
candidate_hypothesis.event_clock: SEC-public filing/issuer announcement establishing the CVR agreement and record date; any later state transition must use its own first-public primary-document timestamp.
candidate_hypothesis.eligibility: US-listed common equity with a primary-filed contractual CVR explicitly attached to each common share, no separate initial trading market, objective record/attachment terms, and auditable state-transition documents.
exclusions: CVRs issued only to merger consideration holders without being stapled to continuing common equity

documentary_points: The payoff is deeply contingent: no voucher had been awarded and no marketing application had been submitted at filing.
Management has no covenant to pursue approval or monetize a voucher and may use or retain it instead.
Payments can be deferred by solvency/dividend-law constraints and may terminate after the contractual deferral period.
Detachment is discretionary and a detached CVR may never develop a trading market.
Additional common shares issued before detachment can carry additional CVRs, diluting per-CVR economics under the aggregate cap.
active_disconfirmation.implication: These features could make the embedded claim economically negligible or too idiosyncratic for a repeatable edge. Independent validation must therefore first establish a sufficiently general event population and contract comparability; failure yields rejection without outcome inspection.

falsification_scope: reject if repository/Legacy evidence shows this is not causally distinct
reject if fewer than a defensible multi-event population can be identified from primary documents
reject if contract heterogeneity prevents ex-ante comparable state definitions
reject if event clocks or attached-right eligibility cannot be established point-in-time
reject before any outcome access if implementability/cost or instrument identity is not auditable
